criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear reef-monitoring purpose and users identified with need explained. Goals implied but objectives/requirements not quantified. References are bare URLs, lacking specific payload performance detail.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt with weekly tasks plus descriptions shows feasible schedule. No robust contingency provision or rationale linking plan to mission, and no explicit planned information-sources list.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Only background reading and tutorials claimed. No results, plots, calculations or STK output shown. Single orbit statement is fundamentally wrong, so no useful technical progress demonstrated.

evidence.quote: My current choice is a geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Logical headings, readable writing, generally consistent formatting. Gantt presented but without caption/number. In-text numbers match URL footnotes, but citations are bare URLs not proper style.

evidence.quote: Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue. Deadlines are indicated by red lines.

technical_issues.issue: Geostationary orbit at 600 km is incorrect; GEO is ~35786 km, 600 km LEO cannot remain fixed above reef.
Editing & Finalisation text says Weeks 7 and 8 reserved but chart shows Weeks 9-10; due 20/11/20 inconsistent with chart ending 16/11.
60% killed in 2016 plus another 50% perished in 2017 exceeds 100% and misrepresents mortality statistics without clarification.

overall: Good mission idea for Australia with feasible schedule, but lacks quantified requirements, source list, and any real technical results, plus major orbit error.

feedback.summary: You presented a promising Great Barrier Reef monitoring concept with clear users and a feasible Gantt schedule. To progress you need quantified requirements, proper sources, corrected orbit choice and real preliminary technical results with professional presentation.
next_steps: Quantify your Mission Concept & Rationale requirements and replace bare URLs with proper references including payload performance for bleaching detection.
Correct your 600 km geostationary orbit in Project Plan & Preliminary Progress and add STK plots/calculations, and align your Weeks 7-8 vs 9-10 text, chart and 20/11/20 due date.
Add explicit information sources, contingency and mission-linked rationale to your plan, and give your Gantt chart a caption/number with proper citation style.

criteria.C1: In Mission Concept & Rationale you clearly identified reef monitoring and users with your near-real-time relay for scientists. For Accomplished, quantify goals and requirements with specific payload literature not bare URLs, and clarify your 60% plus 50% mortality figures which exceed 100%.
criteria.C2: In Project Plan & Preliminary Progress your weekly Gantt with descriptions shows you can complete the work. For Accomplished, add contingencies, explain why the plan fits your reef mission, list planned information sources, and fix Weeks 7-8 vs 9-10 and due-date mismatch.
criteria.C3: You stated a 600 km geostationary orbit and STK tutorials 1-4 in Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, but 600 km cannot be geostationary. For higher levels, correct the orbit and show real results like calculations or STK output with interpretation.
criteria.C4: Your report uses logical headings and readable writing, and you explained gold/blue/red in your Gantt. For Accomplished, add figure caption/number, keep formatting consistent, and use proper in-text citations matching a reference list instead of bare URLs.
